meta.name: Salesforce Certified Data Cloud Consultant
meta.notes: Initial Salesforce Data Cloud Consultant pack — covers solution overview (CDP unification), ingestion patterns (Salesforce CRM connector vs Ingestion API vs file import), the DLO → DMO harmonization model, identity resolution (match rules vs reconciliation rules), Calculated Insights aggregations, segment refresh scheduling, activation targets, Data Actions for real-time triggers, and Data Spaces for tenancy partitioning. Correct-answer distribution balanced 3/3/3/3 across positions.

questions.question: A retail company wants to unify customer data from Marketing Cloud, Service Cloud, Commerce Cloud, and a Snowflake data warehouse into a single profile that can drive personalization and paid-media segments. Which Salesforce product is purpose-built for this workload?
options: Marketing Cloud Personalization (formerly Interaction Studio)
Salesforce Data Cloud
Customer 360 Truth ID
MuleSoft Composer
questions.explanation: Data Cloud is the customer data platform that unifies data across Salesforce clouds and external sources such as Snowflake or S3 into a single Unified Individual profile, then activates segments to marketing and advertising targets. Marketing Cloud Personalization delivers 1:1 web and mobile personalization but is not the cross-source unification layer. Customer 360 Truth ID was a lightweight cross-org ID service that has been superseded by Data Cloud's Identity Resolution. MuleSoft Composer is a no-code integration builder for point-to-point automations, not a CDP.

questions.question: You must ingest 5 million historical orders one time from a legacy on-premises database and continue receiving new orders in near real time from the same source. Which Data Cloud ingestion combination fits?
options: Two separate Data Kits — one Retail Data Kit, one Custom Data Kit
A single Streaming API data stream — historical rows backfill automatically
A batch data stream scheduled every 15 minutes to cover both history and new rows
A one-time file (or S3 bulk) import for history plus an Ingestion API data stream for ongoing updates
questions.explanation: For a large one-time historical load, the file-based bulk import (or S3 batch load) is the right tool; ongoing near-real-time updates should be sent through the Ingestion API, which supports both streaming and bulk endpoints from external systems. A Streaming API stream alone does not automatically backfill years of history. A 15-minute batch is not near real time and would still need a way to load the initial 5M rows efficiently. Data Kits bundle prebuilt schema, segments, and insights — they are not an ingestion mechanism.

questions.question: Which Data Cloud ingestion connector should be chosen to capture incremental changes on Contact and Account records from a Salesforce CRM org without writing custom code?
options: The Salesforce CRM Connector data stream
The Ingestion API in bulk mode
Marketing Cloud Connect
A MuleSoft Composer scheduled flow
questions.explanation: The Salesforce CRM Connector is the native, no-code data stream that captures inserts, updates, and deletes from a Salesforce org's standard and custom objects, using change data capture where available. The Ingestion API requires an external caller to push payloads and is meant for non-Salesforce systems. Marketing Cloud Connect is a Sales/Service Cloud to Marketing Cloud sync — not a Data Cloud ingestion path. MuleSoft Composer would require you to hand-build the sync rather than relying on the certified connector.

questions.question: In Data Cloud's data model, what is the difference between a Data Lake Object (DLO) and a Data Model Object (DMO)?
options: A DLO is a real-time streaming source and a DMO is a batch source
A DLO stores unified individuals and a DMO stores raw ingested rows
A DLO holds raw ingested rows landed from a data stream, and a DMO is the mapped, harmonized entity aligned to the Customer 360 Data Model
A DLO is a segment output table and a DMO is an activation target
questions.explanation: Every data stream lands its rows into a Data Lake Object — a raw, source-shaped table stored in the lake. The consultant then maps DLO fields into a Data Model Object (Individual, Contact Point Email, Sales Order, and so on), which is the harmonized shape consumed by Identity Resolution, Calculated Insights, and segmentation. DLOs are not defined by real-time vs batch — both streaming and batch data streams write to a DLO. Segment membership lives in segment tables, not DLOs, and activations publish externally rather than into an object.

questions.question: While mapping a DLO called `RawContact` to the `Individual` DMO, you find the source has both `first_name` and `given_name` columns holding the same value. What is the recommended action?
options: Rename `given_name` to `first_name` in the source system so only one column exists
Map only one of the two columns to `First Name` on `Individual` and leave the other unmapped
Concatenate the two columns using a formula field on the DMO
Map both columns to `First Name` and let Data Cloud pick the longer value at query time
questions.explanation: A DMO attribute can only be mapped from one DLO field per data stream — mapping the same target twice is not permitted, and there is no query-time pick-longer semantic. Rewriting the upstream source is outside the consultant's scope and unnecessary; the redundant column can simply stay unmapped in Data Cloud. Formula fields on DMOs are useful when combining distinct source values, but choosing a formula when a single column already carries the value adds needless complexity.

questions.question: A retailer wants Data Cloud to treat two records as the same person when they share an exact email address OR when first name, last name, and normalized postal code all match. Where is this logic configured?
options: In the segment's include-criteria filter tree
In a Calculated Insight expression joining the two DLOs
In a Data Action triggered on Individual insert
In an Identity Resolution ruleset's match rules
questions.explanation: Identity Resolution rulesets contain match rules — the logic that decides which source records represent the same individual, including exact and fuzzy strategies combined with OR/AND. Segment filters operate on the already-unified individual, not on how records are unified. Calculated Insights compute metrics and do not unify identities. Data Actions fire outbound events on DMO changes and are not the place to define matching.

questions.question: In an Identity Resolution ruleset, what is the specific role of reconciliation rules (as distinct from match rules)?
options: To decide, once records are matched, how conflicting attribute values are resolved into a single value on the Unified Individual
To decide which two records represent the same person
To publish the Unified Individual to an activation target
To trigger a webhook when a new identity is resolved
questions.explanation: Match rules find same-person records; reconciliation rules decide, for each attribute on the Unified Individual, which source value wins when matched source records disagree — for example "Most Recent Updated" for phone or a source-priority ranking that trusts the home org over marketing data. Publishing to activation targets is done by Activations, not by reconciliation rules. Webhooks on identity change belong to Data Actions.

questions.question: A marketing team wants to segment on "customers whose average order value across the last 90 days exceeds $250." What Data Cloud construct is the correct primary tool?
options: A Data Action that computes the value on each order insert
A Segment filter using a raw DLO field
A Calculated Insight defined as an aggregation grouped by Individual
A Data Stream schedule set to 90 days
questions.explanation: Calculated Insights are Data Cloud's aggregation layer: they define SQL-style GROUP BY expressions (per-individual averages, sums, counts, ratios) that refresh on a schedule and can be referenced directly in segment filters. Data Actions are event-driven outbound triggers, not aggregation compute. Segment filters compare attribute values but do not perform multi-row aggregations of their own — they consume the metrics that a Calculated Insight publishes. A data stream schedule controls ingestion cadence, not per-individual aggregation.

questions.question: When publishing a segment for use in daily marketing campaigns, which refresh cadence is the appropriate configuration?
options: Streaming refresh — the segment recomputes on every ingested row
Scheduled refresh (for example every 12 or 24 hours) aligned to when downstream activations need fresh membership
On-demand refresh only — the consultant refreshes manually before each campaign send
Refresh disabled — segments recompute automatically when their underlying DLO is updated
questions.explanation: Segments in Data Cloud are refreshed either manually (Publish Now) or on a schedule; the schedule cadence should match how fresh the downstream activation must be — typically once or twice a day for standard email campaigns. Streaming refresh is not a segment property (streaming semantics belong to Data Actions and real-time DMOs). Manual-only refresh is fragile for a daily send. Segments do not silently recompute whenever an underlying DLO updates.

questions.question: A brand runs paid-media campaigns on Google Ads and Facebook, emails through Marketing Cloud Engagement, and also wants a snapshot of the current segment membership dropped into an S3 bucket for its data-science team. From Data Cloud, which mechanism sends the same segment to all four destinations?
options: Four separate Data Streams
Four Data Actions
A single Calculated Insight published to each destination
Four Activations of the same segment — one per activation target
questions.explanation: Activations are the mechanism that publishes a segment's membership plus its selected attributes to an external activation target such as Google Ads, Meta, Marketing Cloud Engagement, LinkedIn, or an S3 bucket. Each destination is configured as its own activation on the same segment. Data Streams are for ingestion, not egress. Data Actions are for real-time DMO change events, not scheduled segment publishing. Calculated Insights compute measures; they do not publish audiences.

questions.question: A service team wants Amazon EventBridge to receive a real-time event every time a high-priority Case is inserted into Data Cloud, so its systems can react in seconds. Which Data Cloud construct fits?
options: A Data Action bound to the Case DMO with an EventBridge target
A Calculated Insight refreshed on schedule
A segment activation to an S3 target
A file-based data stream running every minute
questions.explanation: Data Actions are the event-driven, near-real-time trigger surface — they fire when rows are inserted or updated in a DMO and can invoke targets such as Amazon EventBridge, webhooks, or Marketing Cloud Journey Builder entry events. Calculated Insights are scheduled aggregations, not events. Segment activations publish membership snapshots on a schedule, not per-row events. A one-minute file-based data stream would still be batch and would not carry per-record trigger semantics.

questions.question: A holding company owns two brands (Coffee Co and Tea Co) and wants their unified individuals, segments, and activations kept isolated inside a single Data Cloud tenancy, while sharing the same subscription. Which Data Cloud feature accomplishes this?
options: Multiple home orgs on one tenancy
A separate Identity Resolution ruleset for each brand
Data Spaces
Salesforce Sandboxes
questions.explanation: Data Spaces are Data Cloud's tenancy-partition feature — each Data Space has its own segments, activations, and (optionally) DMO scopes, so multiple brands can co-exist inside one Data Cloud tenant without leaking audience data across each other. A Data Cloud tenant has only one home (primary) org; multiple home orgs are not a way to isolate brands. Identity Resolution rulesets partition matching logic but do not isolate the DMO data, segments, or activations themselves. Salesforce Sandboxes clone a Salesforce org for CRM development — they are not a Data Cloud tenancy feature.
